newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece says plane aborts landing at Tirana airport.
newsitem.headline: Greece says plane aborts landing at Tirana airport.

text.p: The captain of an Olympic Airways airplane said he was forced to abort a landing at Tirana airport on Wednesday because it was closed and a Greek government spokesman said shots had been fired.
"We were approaching the airport and it was closed but I went ahead thinking I could still land. But I was unable to contact the control tower and so I turned back," the captain told reporters.
A Greek foreign ministry spokesman told television the landing was aborted because gunfire was heard at the airport.
"There was gunfire at Tirana airport and the landing was not possible," foreign ministry spokesman Costas Bikas told Greek television.

The plane left Athens at 1430 GMT on a special flight to collect the Greek ambassador in the Albanian capital but turned back and landed on the Greek island of Corfu, Athens airport officials told Reuters.

The ambassador was scheduled to be fly to Corfu to join a Greek relief navy ship, which will arrive at the southern Albanian port of Sarande on Thursday to deliver food and medicine, foreign ministry officials said.

An armed insurgency in south Albania, sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes, has spread across the country, with rebels looting a military base on Wednesday only 55 km (34 miles) from Tirana.
